title: Sustaining Plasticity via Learnable Wavelet Activations in Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.12874v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Plasticity loss has emerged as a critical challenge in continual learning that significantly hinders the acquisition of sequential tasks. While optimizing activation designs offers a potential solution, current fixed-form functions suffer from an inherent spectral bias towards low-frequency variations, whereas learnable variants permit unconstrained updates that induce catastrophic forgetting. To address these limitations, we propose a novel learnable wavelet activation that decomposes the activation function into low-frequency and high-frequency components to explicitly counter spectral bias. Furthermore, we employ dynamic wavelet injection to adaptively enhance plasticity for new tasks, alongside a regularization strategy to ensure the stability of previous learned knowledge. Theoretically, we provide rigorous mathematical guarantees for the proposed framework, proving the structural necessity of the hybrid wavelet architecture for eff

translated_title: 持续学习中通过可学习小波激活维持可塑性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12874v1 公告类型：新 摘要：可塑性损失已成为持续学习中的一个关键挑战，显著阻碍了顺序任务的获取。虽然优化激活设计提供了潜在解决方案，但当前固定形式的函数存在对低频变化的固有谱偏差，而可学习变体允许无约束更新，从而引发灾难性遗忘。为解决这些限制，我们提出了一种新颖的可学习小波激活，将激活函数分解为低频和高频组件，以明确对抗谱偏差。此外，我们采用动态小波注入来自适应增强新任务的可塑性，并结合正则化策略确保先前学习知识的稳定性。理论上，我们为所提框架提供了严格的数学保证，证明了混合小波架构在有效应对可塑性损失中的结构必要性。
tldr: 本文提出一种可学习小波激活函数，通过分解低频和高频组件并动态注入，以对抗谱偏差并维持持续学习中的可塑性，同时提供理论保证。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a learnable wavelet activation that decomposes into low/high-frequency components with dynamic injection to counter spectral bias and sustain plasticity in continual learning, backed by theoretical guarantees.
